original_record.question: The diagram shows a solid with six triangular faces. At each vertex there is a number and two of the numbers are 1 and 5, as shown. For each face the sum of the numbers at the three vertices of each face is calculated, and all the sums are the same. What is the sum of all five numbers at the vertices? <image1>
original_record.solution: Let the numbers at two of the other vertices be $u$ and $v$, as shown in the diagram on the right. The three faces sharing the vertex labelled with the number 1 all have the same sum. Then $1+v+u=1+5+u$ and so $v=5$.  Similarly, $1+v+5=1+v+u$ so $u=5$. Hence the sum for each face is $1+5+5$, i.e. 11 , and we see that the number at the bottom vertex is 1 . The total of all the  ![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2023_12_27_0f4ed2787981bb911326g-098.jpg?height=294&width=348&top_left_y=504&top_left_x=1482) vertices is $1+5+5+5+1=17$.
